title: AI chatbots are becoming political advisers. Their answers can mislead voters
content: Millions of Americans are turning to AI for election information, but chatbots are getting voting facts wrong and recommending candidates, raising concerns they could influence voters' decisions.

title: Is America really that polarized? The answer might be a surprise
content: The U.S. has become more politically polarized, but research shows people overestimate their differences and there is 'messy middle' majority of Americans who share overlapping political views.

title: Judge accuses DOJ of 'weaponization,' tosses case against ex-FBI officials
content: The judge said he was "deeply troubled" by the mistakes and rushed nature of the case over the FBI's Hunter Biden probes — one of several politically charged DOJ actions ahead of the midterms.

title: The Supreme Court rejects a DOJ push to separate California ballots
content: The U.S. Supreme Court has denied a last-minute request from the Department of Justice to wade into its unprecedented feud with California over the state's voter rolls.

title: Haley Stevens backs Mike Rogers. And, Gulf states brace for potential attack on Iran
content: Democrats in Michigan are considering their options after Haley Stevens endorsed GOP candidate Mike Rogers for Senate. And the Gulf states are bracing for a possible U.S. attack on Iran after the midterms.

title: Two economists studied California's billionaire tax. They reached wildly different conclusions
content: What happens in California could shape how America taxes the superrich. But will its billionaire tax fill state coffers — or drain them?

title: How does this fluoride-free toothpaste compare when it comes to oral health?
content: Many people are swapping out their fluoride dental products for ones made with a mineral called hydroxyapatite. What do dentists say about it?

title: 6 things to watch for on election night
content: Some of the key storylines to watch will center around various voters groups that have soured on President Trump during his second turn out.

title: With students scarce, college admissions offices get friendlier, less intimidating
content: Colleges are trying to transform an admissions process that has often been daunting, secretive and stressful into an experience that's open, easier — and downright friendly.

title: When it comes to election pressure, this year's Georgia or Michigan could be anywhere
content: The districts that will decide control of the House and Senate next year are spread across the country. Voting officials in those places may face scrutiny and pressure they've never experienced.
